quest.title: The Causality of the Sabzeruz Festival
quest.description: The samsara of the Sabzeruz Festival continues. Are you really getting close to the truth?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x18000, Adventurer's Experience x7, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

chapter.title: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Um...

choices.text: We aren't in a time loop...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! Then the beep we hear every night could just be indicating the deletion of our memories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's why when we wake up, everyone thinks the Sabzeruz Festival hasn't happened yet. It's already the next day, but everyone still thinks it's the day before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But muscle memory can't be erased. That's why Dehya has been getting better at using her greatsword! Now everything makes sense!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Hm, a brilliant deduction.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida, tell us if we're right or wrong!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: To put it simply, it's as if you've mistaken a Pyro Crystalfly for a Firefly in the night. You lost sight of its true nature because you focused too much on your perception that it glows.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That isn't simple at all!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Still the wrong conclusion, huh...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Why don't you go talk to Miss Dehya again? You might learn something new.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right... She did help us find our latest clue, after all. Let's go!

choices.text: Instead, our memories are being erased at the end of each day.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...There you are. Really took me a while to find you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As expected, Dehya also didn't get hurt today.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Get hurt? Why would I? Don't underestimate me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you're still getting used to your new greatsword...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Truth be told, I also think it's pretty strange. It just suddenly felt so familiar in my hands... Wait a sec, how did you know I got a new greatsword to begin with? I didn't tell anyone about it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Traveler, could you explain the situation to her today? Paimon's gotten a little sick of doing it...

choices.text: We don't actually need to explain everything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that works.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You suddenly became proficient with your greatsword because...

choices.text: We've lived through this same day many times already.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...What happened to you guys while I was gone? Did you get brainwashed by some cult?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm, don't think too hard about it. Just take what we're saying at face value.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Alright then. Let me get this straight. You're telling me that my body's already gotten used to this greatsword, but my brain just doesn't remember it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, your memory's being erased every day.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Then I'd have to disagree. That's impossible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Why do you think that?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: If we've actually been reliving the Sabzeruz Festival day after day, then what happened to the things we used, the money we spent, the food we ate?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Common sense says my wallet should've emptied itself a long time ago. There's no way I wouldn't have noticed that.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I've thought about that, too.

choices.text: But if the sages were behind this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right... They could use the Akasha to record what everyone did that day, and then use the city's resources to replenish everything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's not very likely, but it's also not impossible.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: No, it is impossible. I've got proof.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have proof? Where?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: *sigh* You two are surprisingly serious about this nonsensical discussion. Fine, I'll play along for a little longer.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Come with me. Miss Dunyarzad, please come along as well. I still can't guarantee that this area is safe.

choices.text: If they utilized the entire city's resources, as well as information supplied by the Akasha...
And our memories of the day are erased every night.
Let's just get straight to the point.

talks.objective: Go and check the evidence Dehya mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: This is it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This a wooden training dummy. What about it?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: See those marks on the dummy? Those are the result of several days' worth of practice.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Let's say the sages didn't replace it every day. Shouldn't it be hacked to pieces by now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true, but what if they did?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Then the sages would have had to reproduce every mark I left during previous training sessions.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm a professional fighter. My martial school has always emphasized the importance of refined control.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The force, angle, and entry point of each strike is calculated and deliberate. That's why I remember every mark on the dummy, as well as my state of mind as I made each strike.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It's just as they say: Each swordsman has their own unique style, and even the same swordsman can't make the same cut twice. It would be impossible to copy these marks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it really impossible? What if they used some fancy machine to carve every single mark?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: People often say that a Kamera's photo can never replace an artist's painting because the former has no spirit to it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The same thing applies here. At a mere glance, I can differentiate carved marks from the results of combat training.

choices.text: ...That makes sense.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Phew... I hope that cleared things up for you? Hey, is this that new Brainsercise game that's been super popular with the scholars lately? It's surprisingly fun.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Anyway, it's getting late. I should escort Miss Dunyarzad to Nilou's stage. See ya later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Welp, back to square one. Is our memory deletion theory also wrong? *sigh*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But at least we've reached some other conclusions in the meantime?

choices.text: We're not in a time loop.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, that's true. So... can we think of any new ideas right now?

choices.text: Let me think...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Strange? Paimon feels like everything's been strange lately...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How come... we've never thought about leaving the city?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Leaving the city... You're right! It's really strange how we never thought of such a simple solution. Many things should become clear if we can confirm the flow of time outside of the city.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't believe it... Did we miss this because we're tunnel-visioning too hard on our other theories, or because we're just too tired?

choices.text: It is really strange.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How about we go back and ask Nahida? Maybe we've forgotten something about leaving the city.

choices.text: We should've thought of this a long time ago.
I suddenly realized that something is strange...
We're not in the real world.
It seems we'll have to abandon this theory...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You're back early today. Did you find something new?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sort of. We're mostly sure now that we're not in a time loop, and we also aren't in the real world. But at the same time, we have a new question...

choices.text: What will happen if we try to leave the city?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Leaving the city... As far as I remember, you've mentioned your plans to do that twice before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We did? But we don't remember anything! What happened after we talked about those plans? What did we say when we got back?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Let me think... I don't think you ever actually told me what the outcome was. Oh — it's probably more accurate to say that both times, you never came back the whole night.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But you two sometimes stay out the entire night anyway, so at the time, I didn't think too much about it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It is true that sometimes we lose track of time during our investigations. Before we know it, it'll already be the next day. But still... neither of us remember anything about leaving town.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Really? That's kinda strange. In theory, I should've already awakened all your memories.

choices.text: Let's try again tomorrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! Something here's definitely fishy. Let's get to the bottom of this tomorrow!
*beep*

choices.text: Maybe this is the key.
Have we ever tried leaving the city?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* How am I supposed to conduct business when I'm not allowed to leave the city?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: I picked all of these from the forest yesterday, so their freshness is guaranteed!

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: This is divine wisdom...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Atten-tion! Any more requests, young soldiers?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We don't have many more festivals to waste. Hurry and find the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...We're still in the same day!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As expected, it's not as simple as we thought.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, you already knew last night that we didn't break out of the samsara! Why didn't you tell us?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Would there have been a point? You would've spent the night with new worries, with tomorrow still out of reach.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In that case... You might as well rest within that brief moment of hope. An opportunity like that doesn't come by often, and I thought it might help you clear your minds.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought the dook-dook did that! Ah, whatever, guess you were looking out for us after all.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehe, of course. In the time we've been together, you two have been everything to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon's flattered and everything, but maybe you're taking things a little fast...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehehe... What I mean is, even though I had asked you to solve this puzzle, you two are still the only ones who can see me and sense my presence.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In other words, if you weren't here, I may as well not exist. That's why you two have been everything to me. Get it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, Nahida's talking about confusing stuff again...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Anyway, that's enough chit-chat. So Traveler, did the new clues yesterday help you gain a new understanding of the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The time loop theory is indeed incorrect.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you scrapping your previous theory?

choices.text: Dehya's fighting skills have been improving.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, you're right. Gosh, how did we not notice that? In a simple time loop, people's physical conditions should also reset.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So, what's your new hypothesis?

choices.text: Dunyarzad's illness has also gotten worse...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe it's Dehya who wants to show us something this time. Two days ago, we were the ones taking her to see Dunyarzad...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Moon, illusions, and lies... What do they all mean?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's happening right now seems to have happened before. This feeling has been getting stronger and stronger...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Grand Sage said, "Go celebrate the birth of that god to your heart's content." Did he mean something more?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dehya sold her greatsword to raise additional funds, and she was injured because she wasn't used to her new weapon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: My mind feels exhausted, even though I haven't done too much thinking. What is going on?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've already experienced the Sabzeruz Festival many times. And... the day of the festival seems to be in a perpetual samsara.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: People in Sumeru don't dream. What a strange phenomenon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, Nahida said, "The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power. It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and it grants knowledge to the people."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mercenaries rely heavily on muscle memory, and Dehya was able to use her experiences to avoid injury in later samsara cycles.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The beep is a prompt tone for Akasha operations. We still hear it every night, even though we removed our Akasha Terminals.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All the bizarre spaces I saw outside the city had one thing in common: a lack of human presence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those spaces remind me of... dreams. Like the one I had in the Avidya Forest, except these have no sign of human presence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those spaces kept disappearing before my eyes, but as soon as that beep sounded, many more spaces materialized.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those dreamscapes kept vanishing, but as soon as that beep sounded, more new spaces appeared.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ..Was that space actually the real world? But wouldn't a real space just randomly disappearing like that be catastrophic?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: My impression is that each day in this samsara only ends at the sound of that beep from the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That should be it... The flow of time is endlessly cycling within one single day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If all our memories of a day are erased at the end of that day, then we would unwittingly relive the same day again and again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We are all in a dream. It isn't that the people of Sumeru don't dream. Rather, the Akasha is taking their dreams from them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It is a manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: And it grants knowledge to the people.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They say that alchemical divination is the Dendro Archon's divine revelation. So then, if Nahida has referred to herself as the Moon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, wasn't "illusions" a hint that we're all dreaming?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, wasn't "illusions" hinting at the Sages' deception of Sumeru's people?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound right... I need to carefully think things through...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm... I can't seem to cohesively piece everything together.
